gc_teacher.text: Fáilte go dtí an Coláiste! Three weeks every summer, the students learn Irish, play games in Irish, and dance a céilí every night. In Irish. Even the arguments.
The céilí dances have grand names. 'The Walls of Limerick'. 'The Siege of Ennis'. 'The Haymakers' Jig'. Mostly they mean everybody spins until somebody falls over.

gc_student1.text: Bean an tí makes us porridge at seven. In Irish. The porridge is not in Irish, but it feels like it.

gc_student2.text: I came here not knowing a word, and now I can say 'can I go to the toilet' and 'where is the céilí'. Which is all you need, honestly.

then.text: Go n-éirí an bád leat! May the boat go well with you. That is our send-off for anything on the water.

else.text: Gweedore is a Gaeltacht, a district where Irish is still the everyday language. Students come here every summer to the coláiste, and teachers fine them for speaking English. Fada, a little line over a letter, matters.
Rás na dTonnta? Our crews will row if you can show me the words. What does bád mean?

then.text: Right! Farraige is the sea, tonn is a wave, rámha is an oar. You have the vocabulary of a crew now. Tell Tory I sent you.

else.text: Close, but not on the water. Ask me again when you have thought about it. Bád is a boat.
Fáilte! The summer students are loud, the teachers louder. Are you here to learn Irish, or just to listen?
